node.system_libraries: /usr/lib/libz.1.dylib, /usr/lib/libc++.1.dylib, /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib, CoreFoundation and Security come with macOS and are not pinned, as for the Rust toolchain.
node.type_stripping: process.features.typescript is "strip". Node runs .ts files directly. No --experimental flag is passed.
node.rule: The node binary, libnode and every Homebrew library above must have these hashes. A Homebrew upgrade that changes any of them is a contract amendment, the same rule as rustc and rustfmt.

npm.tree_algorithm: som-rs/tests/typescript-output-v1/tree_sha.py: for each path in sorted(root.rglob("*")), a symlink adds <relpath>\0symlink:<target>\n, a regular file adds <relpath>\0<sha256>\n; the tree sha is the SHA-256 of all lines.

formatter.invocation: node node_modules/prettier/bin/prettier.cjs --check --no-config --no-editorconfig . in the product directory
formatter.configuration: prettier defaults. Products contain no .prettierrc, .prettierignore, .editorconfig or prettier key in package.json; --no-config and --no-editorconfig keep files above the product directory out.
formatter.applies: Every product file that prettier formats: the .ts, .tsx, .css, .html, .json and .md files, generated or fixed. node_modules is ignored by prettier's defaults.
formatter.rule: Every product file is already in the formatter's output, so the format_check command accepts the product unchanged. The fixed files are formatted reference bytes; the reference renderer writes the generated files in that format.
formatter.sha256_rule: The SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, no spaces) {"node": <node.sha256>, "libnode": <node.libnode.sha256>, "prettier_tree_sha256": <tree sha of the vendored prettier package>}. It is the React bundle formatter asset.
formatter.prettier_tree_rule: tree_sha.py of node_modules/prettier after the install command, from the vendored cache; 56 files, 0 symlinks

packages.registry: https://registry.npmjs.org, accessed once before the freeze (approved on 2026-10-22, issue #68) to fill the vendored npm cache and write the lockfile. Every install after that is offline.
packages.lock: reference/package-lock.json, lockfileVersion 3, written by that download and frozen with this contract
packages.transitive: Every other package comes from the lockfile. lock_packages lists each lockfile package with its version, integrity and flags, and whether the vendored cache holds its tarball.
packages.platform_packages: The lockfile lists the optional platform packages of @rolldown/binding-*, lightningcss-* and fsevents for every platform. The vendored cache holds only those npm fetched for aarch64-apple-darwin; npm ci skips the others on this host. Phase 1 supports this host only.
packages.install_scripts: fsevents is the only lockfile package with hasInstallScript. The install command passes --ignore-scripts, so no package script runs.

vendored_cache.rule: Written once by the approved download, then read-only (chmod -R a-w). A new download goes to a new numbered path.
vendored_cache.logs: The download wrote its debug logs to .local/react-output/npm-logs-download-001 through npm_config_logs_dir, and every command sets npm_config_logs_dir outside the cache, so the tree hash stays fixed.

commands.environment: PATH=<node bin dir>:/usr/bin:/bin, npm_config_cache=<vendored cache>, npm_config_offline=true, npm_config_audit=false, npm_config_fund=false, npm_config_update_notifier=false, npm_config_logs_dir=<a directory outside the vendored cache>, npm_config_userconfig=<an empty file>. npm is <node.binary> <npm.root>/bin/npm-cli.js. The offline settings keep npm off the network; the other commands are not sandboxed, and none of them is configured to use the network.
commands.build: node node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js build --outDir <dist dir outside the product> --emptyOutDir
commands.build_reproducible: build runs twice into two new directories; the two trees are byte-identical.
commands.lock_unchanged: package.json and package-lock.json bytes after the commands equal the generated files.
commands.product_unchanged: Every product file outside node_modules has the same bytes after the commands as before them, and no product file outside node_modules is added or removed.
commands.runner: som-rs/tests/react-output-v1/run_gates.py runs these commands in this order on a fresh copy of a product and writes the gate evidence.

postgresql.cluster: A fresh initdb cluster per acceptance run, on a QA port other than 8765 and 18765, with UTF8 encoding and UTC time zone.
postgresql.start: pg_ctl start runs with LC_ALL=C. Without it the postmaster can stop with "postmaster became multithreaded during startup" on this host.
postgresql.use: Only for the Python service in the API contract runs; the React product has no database.

python.use: The Python service in the API contract runs (som-rs/runtime/acceptance-m3-venv), and the contract scripts.

reference_verification.rule: The contract records a reference product (public product 003, a som.prompt.v4 prompt rendered by render_reference.py) that passes every gate of commands against the vendored cache, builds twice to identical dist trees with the lockfile and the vendored cache unchanged, and passes the API contract against the hosted Python product of the same prompt. The same run covers the eight public v1 to v4 products.
reference_verification.result: install, typecheck, format_check, test, build-1 and build-2 exit 0 on a fresh copy for each of the products 000, 119, 001, 120, 002, 121, 003 and 122; both builds are identical; the lockfile, every product file outside node_modules and the vendored cache tree are unchanged; the API contract records all 20 steps against the hosted Python product, with no failed step and with exactly the steps whose when condition is false skipped.
reference_verification.name_cases_result: The nine target-examples.json name cases render and pass install, typecheck, format_check, test and two identical builds with the lockfile, every product file outside node_modules and the vendored cache unchanged. RN07 (a v3 filter field named valueOf) first failed typecheck: listRows had the default parameter ListQuery = {}, and {} is not assignable to a ListQuery whose valueOf member is a boolean. reference/src/api.ts now takes the query without a default, and every run in this record used the fixed file. The API contract does not run for name cases.
